item.title: Ryan Routh convicted: Donald Trump assassination plotter tries to stab himself in court; daughter shouts ‘rigged’ trial
item.description: Ryan Routh was convicted for plotting to assassinate Donald Trump and then attempted to stab himself in the neck with a pen in court. The incident occurred after the jury's verdict, prompting intervention by US Marshals. Routh faces a life sentence, while his daughter was removed from the courtroom after protesting the proceedings.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: ‘Without China, Russia is nothing’: Volodymyr Zelenskyy says Beijing could pressure Moscow to end war; criticizes silence
item.description: President Zelenskyy urged the UN Security Council that China possesses the leverage to pressure Russia into ending the war in Ukraine, highlighting Beijing's significant influence over Moscow. Despite China's claims of neutrality and calls for peace, Zelenskyy criticized its continued economic support for Russia and alleged involvement of Chinese nationals in the conflict.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: ‘Evil plan?' Elon Musk's father accused of sexually abusing children and stepchildren for decades; Errol Musk denies claims as 'false'
item.description: Errol Musk, father of Elon Musk, faces accusations of sexual abuse. The allegations span from 1993 and involve multiple children and stepchildren. Investigations were launched, but outcomes vary. Errol Musk denies the claims, alleging fabrication and extortion attempts. Elon Musk has previously described his father negatively and is currently estranged. Maye Musk also accused Errol of abuse in her memoir.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: ‘Surrender to ransom demands’: Donald Trump condemns recognition of Palestinian state by West; warns it 'rewards Hamas'
item.description: Donald Trump criticized Western nations' recognition of a Palestinian state, deeming it a reward for Hamas's "horrible atrocities." He argued such recognitions embolden the group, fuel conflict, and distract from securing hostage releases. Trump, deeply involved in ceasefire efforts, accused Hamas of obstructing peace and is set to meet with Muslim-majority leaders to discuss the Gaza crisis and post-war governance.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 'Aimless war': Donald Trump says Ukraine 'in position to win' with US, NATO support; calls Russia 'paper tiger'
item.description: Donald Trump has asserted that Ukraine, backed by the EU and NATO, could potentially reclaim its territory, criticizing Russia's war effort as 'aimless'. He highlighted Russia's economic struggles, suggesting Ukraine should act now. Trump also supports NATO shooting down Russian jets violating their airspace, affirming a strong stance towards the alliance, while remaining non-committal on direct US action.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 'I do': Donald Trump supports Nato shooting down Russian jets violating airspace; stops short of committing US forces
item.description: Amid rising tensions over the Ukraine war, Donald Trump urged NATO nations to shoot down Russian planes violating their airspace. While meeting with Volodymyr Zelenskyy, Trump emphasized NATO's strength but remained noncommittal on direct U.S. action. Recent airspace violations, including incidents in Estonia and Poland, have heightened concerns.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Florida assassination attempt: Ryan Routh found guilty of attempting to kill Donald Trump; US President hails 'meticulously handled' trial
item.description: Ryan Routh was found guilty by a jury for attempting to assassinate Donald Trump at his Florida golf club. Routh, who defended himself, faced multiple federal charges related to the incident. Prosecutors argued Routh meticulously planned the attack, while Routh claimed a crime didn't occur as he never pulled the trigger.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: ‘Gotta catch 'em all’: DHS goes viral with Pokémon-themed immigration arrest video-Watch
item.description: The US Department of Homeland Security released a Pokémon-themed video showcasing arrests of undocumented immigrants, sparking controversy with its "Gotta Catch 'Em All" slogan and use of the animated series' visuals. The video, featuring mugshots displayed as Pokémon cards, has garnered over 40 million views on X, raising concerns about copyright infringement and the agency's messaging amid increased deportation efforts.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Nobel Prize for Donald Trump? Emmanuel Macron sets one condition; what he said
item.description: Emmanuel Macron stated that Donald Trump's Nobel Peace Prize hinges on resolving the Israeli-Palestinian conflict in Gaza. Trump claimed to have ended seven wars, including conflicts involving India and Pakistan, asserting his deservingness of the prize for each. Despite endorsements from some nations, the Nobel Committee maintains its selection is based solely on merit.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: UAE: World’s biggest AI film contest announced with $1 million prize, here's how creators can register
item.description: Dubai is set to host the world's largest AI Film Award as part of the 1 Billion Followers Summit in January 2026, offering a $1 million grand prize. Global creators are invited to use Google Gemini tools to produce short films exploring themes of future visions or hidden stories. The competition aims to democratize filmmaking and highlight AI's creative potential.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: ‘Ill-timed and insensitive’: Nexstar Media Group will not air Jimmy Kimmel Live! to focus on ‘market-relevant’ programmes
item.description: Leading US broadcast station owners Nexstar and Sinclair are preempting the return of 'Jimmy Kimmel Live!' following controversial remarks made by Kimmel about conservative activist Charlie Kirk. Nexstar cited Kimmel's 'ill-timed and insensitive' comments, emphasizing a commitment to respectful dialogue. While Nexstar and Sinclair will not air the show, it remains available on Disney's streaming platforms.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: ‘Embarrassing’: Donald Trump struggles to pronounce acetaminophen; repeats unproven link between drug and autism
item.description: President Trump struggled to pronounce "acetaminophen" (Tylenol) while baselessly linking it to autism, advising pregnant women to limit its use. Social media mocked his mispronunciation and unscientific claim. The WHO refuted Trump's assertion, clarifying that neither Tylenol nor vaccines cause autism, emphasizing the safety and life-saving impact of childhood immunizations.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: ‘Do the right thing!’ Donald Trump refuses to meet with Democrats over ‘unserious’ demands; senate leaders say he’s 'chickening out"
item.description: Donald Trump has cancelled a meeting with Democratic congressional leaders, accusing them of making unrealistic demands regarding budget negotiations. Trump claims Democrats are pushing for over $1 trillion in new spending, including controversial policies on healthcare and immigration. He criticized their attempts to cut the Rural and Vulnerable Hospital Fund.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 'Dr' Donald Trump, Tylenol, and why Americans don't trust the 'science' anymore
item.description: Tylenol, or to use its generic name paracetamol, was in the news recently when Donald Trump suddenly put on his ‘Doctor’ cap and claimed that acetaminophen, the active ingredient in Tylenol, was causing autism, warned pregnant women to avoid the drug, and said the USFDA would include warnings for its use — much to the chagrin of scientific consensus. The problem, however, is that Americans no longer ‘trust the science’. Much like with the Democrats, Americans have had a very messy break-up with scientific consensus — and some of it is thanks to “Dr” Trump, but also because of the mendacious propaganda that passed itself off as science.
item.dc:creator: Nirmalya Dutta

item.title: “It’s a great country”: Cristiano Ronaldo praises Saudi Arabia as he celebrates kingdom’s 95th National Day
item.description: Cristiano Ronaldo celebrated Saudi Arabia’s 95th National Day with a heartfelt message, praising the country’s culture, safety, and lifestyle. Living in Saudi Arabia with his family, he’s committed both on and off the pitch. With 103 goals for Al-Nassr and just 55 shy of 1,000 career goals, Ronaldo’s focus remains on winning titles and building a lasting legacy.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 'I am waiting on street': French president Macron calls Trump after NYC police stop him - watch video
item.description: During the UN General Assembly session in New York City, French President Emmanuel Macron's convoy was halted due to traffic restrictions implemented for US President Donald Trump's motorcade. A video shows Macron waiting on the sidewalk, with a New York police officer apologizing for the delay.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Saudi Arabia signs game-changing deal to launch flying cars and air taxis
item.description: Saudi Arabia is poised to revolutionize urban transportation with flying cars. Front End and Cluster 2 Airports have partnered with EHang to introduce autonomous aerial vehicles. This initiative aims to deploy passenger air taxis and cargo drones, manage urban air traffic, and establish local manufacturing.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Canadian outdoor brand Arc’teryx faces backlash over fireworks in the Himalayas: Art, climate, and controversy
item.description: A collaborative fireworks display in the Himalayas by Cai Guo-Qiang and Arc'teryx has ignited controversy. The "Rising Dragon" event, staged on a Tibetan plateau, drew criticism for its potential environmental impact on the fragile ecosystem. Both Arc'teryx and Cai Guo-Qiang have issued apologies, and Chinese authorities have launched an investigation into the event's ecological impact and approval process.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: UNGA security breach? Network that could cripple telecoms busted; 100k SIMs seized
item.description: Ahead of the United Nation General Assembly, US Secret Service and NYPD took down a device network. This network operated in the tri-state area. It could cripple telecom systems. Over 300 SIM card servers and 100,000 SIM cards were recovered. These devices could conduct telecommunications attacks. The devices were near the UN General Assembly.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: What's the Rapture? Christian prophecy sparks buzz about 'end-time' event - explained
item.description: Social media is abuzz with predictions of the Christian Rapture, fueled by South African pastor Joshua Mhlakela's claim that Jesus will return on September 23 and 24, 2025. This has ignited viral discussions and humorous takes online.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk
